loops.minute_1: Player discovers simple horizontal paddle control. First brick destroyed: immediate reward (visible points, brick removal, audio). Loop: control → collision → destruction → score gain.
loops.minute_10: 2-3 bricks destroyed. Player experiments with paddle impact zones to alter rebound angle. First tension moments: ball approaching bottom, player must adjust position quickly. Feedback loop: each brick = cumulative score. Difficulty begins to increase (ball speed accelerates).
loops.hour_5: Second wall reached. Paddle reduced to half-size, ball speed increased (after 4 hits, 12 hits, orange/red row contact). Sustained concentration required. Multiple attempts to beat personal high score (replay motivated by score comparison). Arcade progression: by player mastery, not unlocks.
loops.endgame: Complete destruction of both walls = victory terminal state. No prestige reset or infinite mode. Replay motivated by challenge: beating personal high score. Game ends decisively.

objectives.victory_condition: Destroy both screens of bricks within 3 allocated lives
objectives.defeat_condition: Miss the ball three consecutive times (lose all lives)
objectives.player_goal: Maximize score while preventing the ball from falling past the paddle

games.retention_answer: Player progression driven by **skill mastery**. Each session improves visual prediction (rebound anticipation, paddle timing). Personal high score becomes metric of progress, motivating replay. Physics is simple and deterministic: clear learning curve ('I hit too left, ball rebounded too steeply'). Difficulty increases mechanically. Core retention: arcade essence—dominate by expertise, not cosmetics.
games.architecture_guess: Deterministic physics engine (seed-stable collision, angle-based rebound). Simple brick state (destroyed=true/false). Score accumulator. Finite level progression (2 walls). Input-agnostic control (paddle position as float 0.0-1.0). No power-ups or cosmetics.

loops.minute_1: Tutorialized interface (swipe to aim, tap to shoot). First brick destroyed with festive animation + satisfying audio. Power-up cascades and is collected immediately. Loop: aim → shoot → destruction → visual/audio reward → next brick visible. Friction minimal, success within 1-2 minutes.
loops.minute_10: 5-10 bricks destroyed. XP bar toward next level fills visibly. Diverse power-ups collected (multiball changes tactics: multiple balls = chaos, more satisfying). Gray 'tough bricks' (multi-hit) discovered; player learns strategy exists. Progression sensation: 'I am 25% through level 5 of 500' → sense of length.
loops.hour_5: Levels ~40-80 on 500+. Brick patterns become asymmetric (strategic gaps, interspersed solid blocks). Power-ups require judgment: use multiball now or save for next level? Cosmetic unlocks appear (rare paddles/balls = status). Leaderboard visible: 'I am rank 2500 globally, but friends are 1800' → competitive pressure.
loops.endgame: Level 500 reached. Game pivots to Survival Mode (no end, infinite score accumulation). Leaderboard becomes primary: global competition, sessions shift to short/daily (15-30min/day vs 30-60min arcade session). Limited-time events (monthly seasons): 'Collect 100 bricks in 7 days to unlock Gold Paddle' → FOMO.

objectives.victory_condition: Clear all bricks on level layout without losing all lives
objectives.defeat_condition: Lose all available lives before clearing bricks
objectives.player_goal: Progress through 500+ levels by destroying brick patterns, collecting power-ups, maximizing score

objectives.defeat_condition: Ball falls past paddle or bricks descend to bottom of screen
objectives.player_goal: Survive as long as possible and climb global leaderboard

games.retention_answer: Retention driven by **cosmetic progression + social competition**, not skill mastery. 500+ levels create illusion of infinite content (200+ hours playtime). Power-ups provide rapid dopamine loops (satisfying collection). Leaderboards + seasonal events generate FOMO: 'if I don't play this week, I miss Gold Paddle skin'. Casual-mobile formula: progression by unlocks, competition by status, retention by time-limited events.
games.architecture_guess: Deterministic physics with cascading power-ups (separate collectible system). Destructible bricks with variable durability (gray=2-3 hits). Level progression (500 stages with unique patterns). Cosmetic unlock system (paddle/ball skins = rarity tier). Leaderboard + seasonal event system. Dual-mode architecture (Stage mode → Survival mode toggle). Session scheduling (daily login bonus).

note: This is an OBSERVATION, not a design prescription. Breakout (1976) establishes core arcade loop (skill progression, deterministic physics). Brick Breaker King demonstrates casual-mobile escalation (cosmetics, social leaderboards, time-limited events). runm_breakout charter explicitly rejects Brick Breaker's progression systems (hors_scope: 'multi-niveaux, tableau scores, persistance'). These observations provide architectural reference points for future expansion decisions, if any. No copy-pasting: understand the assembly, don't replicate the game.
